elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: the Company owns and shall retain all right, title and interest in and to (i) the Site and all other deliverables and work product created by or for HDI for the Company

elements.element: Vendor assigns such deliverables/work product to Customer
elements.evidence: HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest it may have in such deliverables and work product
HDI retains all right, title and interest in its pre-existing intellectual property

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: (ii) all user, customer, order and transaction data ... and the Company retains all rights in the Company Data
Nothing in this Agreement creates any joint ownership of intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: insertion addresses only pre-existing IP; no reference to generic tools or know-how

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables
elements.evidence: licence is limited to embedded HDI IP and omits worldwide, use, modify, sublicense

reasons: All atomic preferred elements are expressly present in the inserted clause 5.5: Customer ownership of the Site/deliverables/work product, Vendor assignment, Vendor retention of pre-existing IP, a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor IP, Customer Data rights, and an express no-joint-ownership statement.
The fallback bargain is not (and need not be) met; no fallback-only rights (worldwide, modify, sublicense) were imported, keeping the levels unmixed.

The clause is a concise insertion filling a genuine gap (the agreement was silent on ownership), with no rewriting of existing sections and no new exceptions; 'Company Data' is defined in-line so no dangling term is created.
